key_insight: The paper defines "continuous-tone simple points" and introduces an ℓ0-norm of a cyclic gradient as a topology-aware measure that can be relaxed for use in data-driven segmentation, enabling topology preservation beyond binary images.
problem_solved: Existing simple-point topology checks are limited to binary images and non-differentiable, preventing integration of topology-preserving constraints into gradient-based deep learning for segmentation and related tasks.
method: Formalize continuous-tone simple points using a cyclic (circular) gradient operator that captures local topological changes in gray-scale images.
Define an ℓ0-norm of the cyclic gradient as a compact topology-sensitive energy and provide a relaxed/approximated formulation suitable for optimization within neural-network training.
Integrate the topology term into segmentation training as a regularizer (or loss component) and validate on tasks where preserving connectivity/holes matters.
impact: Provides a practical way to enforce topology-aware constraints in end-to-end learning, improving structural consistency (connectivity, holes, thin structures) in segmentation and related image-analysis tasks important for medical imaging, remote sensing, and shape analysis.
visual_elements: Schematic of the cyclic gradient neighborhood around a pixel showing how topology changes are detected
Before/after segmentation comparison highlighting preserved vs. broken topology (e.g., connected vessels or holes)
Block diagram of a segmentation network with an added topology loss term derived from the ℓ0 of cyclic gradient
Metric chart showing topology metrics (e.g., connectivity or Betti numbers) and segmentation quality versus baseline
paper_title: Continuous-tone Simple Points: An $\ell_0$-Norm of Cyclic Gradient for Topology-Preserving Data-Driven Image Segmentation
paper_authors: Wenxiao Li, Faqiang Wang, Yuping Duan, Li Cui, Liqiang Zhang
